- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast highs by 2–5%.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak.
- In low-sentiment periods, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast tends to underestimate downward moves; adjust downward by 3–8% for 3–5 day lags.
- If sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., 0.2–0.4), model overreacts; dampen forecast growth by 10–20% in early days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — smooth out forecast curves using 3-day moving average to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model tends to overpredict — apply a 5–10% downward bias to all 30d forecasts.
